p0.original: 关键问题：我们的行为如何受到社会情境的影响
p0.en: Key issue: How our behaviour is influenced by social circumstances

p2.original: 我们的行为通常要符合社会情境，当面对不熟悉、不明确的情境时，我们会参考他人的行为。
p2.en: Our behaviour is usually in line with social circumstances, and when faced with unfamiliar and unclear circumstances, we refer to the behaviour of others.

p3.original: 想象一下，在一次非常棒的暑期工作面试中，你发现自己有可能被谷歌公司聘为实习生。在面试过程中，面试官讲了一个低俗的笑话去打破沉默，你觉得这种行为很无礼。
p3.en: Imagine, in a very good summer job interview, you found yourself at risk of being hired as an intern by Google. During the interview, the interviewer gave a cheap joke to break the silence, which you found rude.

p4.original: 你会直接表达你的感受，还是会用大笑掩饰？面试结束后，他提议与你一起在公司食堂吃午餐。
p4.en: Will you express your feelings directly or will you cover it up with a big smile? After the interview, he offered to have lunch with you in the company cafeteria.

p5.original: 午餐时，你会主动与对方交谈，还是会等待他引出话题？
p5.en: Will you talk to each other voluntarily at lunch or will you wait for him to bring up the subject?

p6.original: 你会先吃掉你最喜欢的甜点，然后再喝不太喜欢的汤吗？
p6.en: Would you eat your favorite dessert and then drink the soup you don't like?

p7.original: 切完肉后，在将切好的食物放到嘴里时，你会将叉子从左手移到右手吗？还是始终将叉子握在左手中？
p7.en: When you're done cutting the meat, and putting the cut food in your mouth, will you move the fork from your left hand to your right hand? Or do you keep the fork in your left hand?

p8.original: 即使在上述简单的社会情境下，也存在许多社会和文化规则来规定什么是恰当的和可以接受的行为。如果正处于这种陌生情境，你就会像大多数人一样，从周围的人那里习得“恰当”的行事风格。在交谈的过程中，面试官摆好餐具，然后你会效仿他，并假装喜欢他那无厘头的笑话。你想要得到这份工作，因此表现得比以前更加顺从。欧洲人不会像美国人一样在吃饭时将餐具转手，这种习惯是通过在家庭环境中观察他人行为时无意识习得的，很少有人被明示要这样做。甜点虽然十分美味诱人，但无论如何它都会排在进餐顺序的最后一步，这是脚本化的行为，意味着在给定的情境下，我们可以按照特定的行为顺序预测性地采取行动，如餐厅或家庭用餐的标准脚本。
p8.en: Even in these simple social circumstances, there are many social and cultural rules that define what is appropriate and acceptable. If you are in this strange situation, you, like most people, will learn from the people around you the “right” style of conduct. During the conversation, the interview officer set up the table, and then you followed him and pretended to like his stupid jokes. You wanted the job, so you acted more submissive than before. Europeans do not switch their food sets like Americans, a habit that is unwittingly learned by observing the behaviour of others in a family environment, and few are explicitly asked to do so. The dessert, though delicious, is tempting, but in any case it will be the last step in the order of meals, which is a scriptic behaviour, which means that in given circumstances we can act predictably in accordance with a given sequence of behaviour, such as a standard script for restaurants or home meals.

p9.original: 当我们融入新的环境时，情境能最大限度地控制人格，其重要性凌驾于我们过去的学习经验、价值观和信念之上。情境越新颖，我们对习惯性反应方式的依赖就越少。我们通过参考他人来判断自己的行为以便他人认可我们。然而，在你第一次去教堂做礼拜或参加葬礼时，或你第一次和兄弟调侃他人以及参加摇滚音乐会时，两种情境中可接受的行为会大相径庭。我们将看到，这些社会环境的压力会对我们的心理产生强大的影响，使我们做出一些我们往常不会做的事情，甚至是不道德和非法的行为。
p9.en: When we are integrated into a new environment, circumstances can exercise maximum control over the human personality, which is important over our past learning experience, values and beliefs. The newer the situation, the less we rely on customary responses. We judge our behaviour by reference to others in order for others to recognize us. However, when you go to church for the first time or to a funeral, or when you first flirt with your brother and go to a rock concert, there will be a great difference in acceptable behaviour between the two situations. We will see that the pressures of these social environments will have a strong psychological impact on us, leading us to do something that we would never have done before, even immorally and illegally.

p10.original: 在米尔格拉姆的服从实验中，当比尔扮演“老师”时，这些压力正在发挥作用，使他对一个无辜的“学生”施加了极其痛苦的电击惩罚。社会角色、情境规则、我们的衣着打扮、是否匿名、是否处于竞争中或者仅仅是他人在场，这些都会极大地影响我们的举止。通常，这些微妙的情境变量会悄无声息地以多种方式影响我们，甚至会使我们做出思虑不周或愚蠢的行为。我们的核心概念强调了这一点：
p10.en: In the subjection experiment of Milgram, when Bill played “teachers”, these pressures were working, causing him to impose an extremely painful electroshock punishment on an innocent “pupil”. The role of society, the rules of the situation, our dress, our anonymity, whether they are in competition or whether they are only in the presence of others will greatly influence our behaviour. Usually, these delicate situational variables affect us in many ways and even lead to poorly thought-out or stupid behaviour. Our core concepts underline this:

p11.original: 我们的行为通常要符合社会情境，当面对不熟悉、不明确的情境时，我们会参考他人的行为。
p11.en: Our behaviour is usually in line with social circumstances, and when faced with unfamiliar and unclear circumstances, we refer to the behaviour of others.

p12.original: 在本部分中，我们将探讨“情境主义”及相关支持研究。情境主义（situationism）假设外部环境或社会环境可以对人们的思想、情感和行为产生微妙而强烈的影响。情境主义与特质主义（dispositionism）相反，后者倾向于将行为归因于内部因素，如基因、人格特质和性格特点。特质主义从个体内部寻找为什么某人以特定方式行事的解释，而情境主义则倾向于探究外部情境。下面让我们更深入地观察在顺从、服从、盲目的群体思维及袖手旁观下，情境力量所造成的危害。
p12.en: In this section, we will look at “situationalism” and related supportive research. The situationalism (situationism) assumes that the external or social environment can have a subtle and powerful influence on people's minds, emotions and behaviour. In contrast to the dictumism, the latter tends to attribute conduct to internal factors, such as genes, personality characteristics and character characteristics. Characterism seeks an explanation from the inside of an individual as to why someone acted in a particular way, while situationalism tends to explore external situations. Let us now look more closely at the harm caused by the forces of the situation, through submission, obedience, blind group thinking and inaction.

p14.en: 11.1 Recall the social determinants of some behaviour.

p15.original: 11.2 评价影响从众和不从众的因素。
p15.en: 11.2 Factors affecting both the public and the private sector.

p16.original: 11.3 解释在各种情境下服从权威的力量。
p16.en: 11.3 Explanation of the power to submit to authority in all circumstances.

p17.original: 11.4 利用米尔格拉姆的研究结果启发人们做出富有同情心的行为。
p17.en: 11.4 Use of the research results of Milgram to inspire compassionate behaviour.

p21.original: 回顾一些行为的社会决定因素。
p21.en: Recall the social determinants of some behaviour.

p22.original: 上文中所描述的谷歌公司的工作面试，为我们提供了一个情境影响行为的例子，你会尝试在未来的雇主面前做“恰当的事”或任何有利于你获得这份工作的事情。当你去比较一个学生与朋友聊天和与教授交谈的方式，或者你同家人聚餐与同朋友一起观看喜爱的电视节目的行为时，就会注意到情境的力量。大多数人都能学会判断自己的社交环境，并使自己的行为适应情境的需求。大多数人的反应在很大程度上都取决于两个因素：他们所扮演的社会角色和该群体的社会规范。接下来我们将仔细探究这两个因素。
p22.en: The Google job interview described above provides us with an example of context-impacting behavior, and you try to do “the right thing” in front of future employers or anything that would help you get this job. When you compare the way a student talks with a friend and with a professor, or you eat with your family and watch with your friends a favorite TV show, you notice the power of the situation. Most people can learn to judge their social environment and adapt their behaviour to the needs of the situation. The response of the majority depends to a large extent on two factors: their social role and the social norms of the group. We will then look closely at both of these factors.

p24.original: 你如何回答“你是谁”这一基本问题？一个答案可能是：我是一名大学生、做兼职、有宗教信仰、常骑自行车、技术人员、优秀学生及相貌较好。这些描述词中的每一个都将成为你在人生舞台上扮演的社会角色。而在关注集体价值大于个体价值的文化中，人们可能会这样回答这个问题：我是一个姐姐，是X族，是Y部落的成员。社会角色（social role）是在给定的情境或群体中人们期望的几种社会定义的行为模式之一。你的兴趣、能力和目标，或者群体及不受你控制的文化、经济或生物条件，都与你扮演的社会角色有关。无论如何，社会角色会规范你的行为，并使你清楚地知道应该做什么、应该如何做、何时何地去做以及为什么这样做。各行各业包括许多角色，如接待员、工会组织者、经理、理赔代理人、技术员等。
p24.en: How do you answer the basic question, "Who are you?" The answer may be: I'm a college student, part-time, religious, cycling, technologist, good student and better looking. Each of these descriptions will be the social role you play on the stage of life. And in a culture that focuses on collective values more than individual values, one might answer the question: I am a sister, an X, a member of the Y tribe. Social role is one of several socially defined modes of behaviour that people expect in given situations or groups. Your interests, abilities and objectives, or groups and cultural, economic or biological conditions outside your control, are all related to the social role you play. In any case, social actors will regulate your behaviour and give you a clear idea of what should be done, how, when and why. The various professions include many actors, such as receptionists, trade unionists, managers, compensation settlement agents, technicians, etc.

p25.original: 你生活和工作的情境还决定了你成为什么样的角色以及其他人对你的期望。例如，大学生这一社会角色隐含的意思是你需要上课、学习和在截止日期之前上交论文。这也意味着一定程度的特权，通常不必全职工作，对改善自己的思维方式有着浓厚的兴趣，并有足够的时间对自己的职业选择进行探索。此外，扮演此角色降低了你扮演其他某些角色的可能性。因此，你作为大学生的角色减少了你以后变成恐怖分子、帮派头目或成为卡车司机的可能性。不过较为成熟的学生可能已经拥有了自己的家庭、从事全职工作、成为退伍老兵或社会政治活动家。
p25.en: The circumstances in which you live and work determine what role you are and what others expect of you. For example, the social role of university students implies that you need to attend classes, study and submit papers before the deadline. It also implies a certain degree of privilege, usually without having to work full-time, a strong interest in improving its own way of thinking and sufficient time to explore its career choices. Besides, playing this role reduces the possibility of you playing some other roles. As a result, your role as a university student reduces the likelihood that you will later become a terrorist, a gang leader or a truck driver. However, more mature students may already have their own family, full-time employment, veterans or socio-political activists.

p26.original: 除了个人扮演的特定社会角色外，群体还制定了许多“不成文的规则”，规定了所有成员应该采取的行动方式。帮派成员可能会无条件地服从其领导人，并愿意与任何指定的“敌人”进行战斗或将其杀害。科技行业的现代男性高管通常穿牛仔裤上班，很少系领带。而在其他工作环境（如保险行业）中，这是错误的着装。作为一种宗教信仰，在有些地区女学生可能会戴着面纱上课，因为在某些文化中必须这样做。意大利人互相问候时，以固定的先左后右的顺序在脸颊上亲吻，而波兰人还要再加一个吻。这些期望，即社会规范（social norms），决定了特定行为环境中恰当的态度和行为。社会规范可以是广泛的指导方针，如关于哪些政治或宗教态度被认为是可以接受的。社会规范也可能非常具体，体现为行为标准，如在图书馆保持安静或参加工作面试时保持皮鞋干净。社会规范甚至可以引导对话，因为社会规范会限制在某些群体面前讨论敏感或禁忌话题，如异性或具有已知政治差异的群体。
p26.en: In addition to the particular social role played by individuals, groups have developed many “unwritten rules” that set out the modalities of action to be taken by all members. Gang members may unconditionally obey their leaders and be willing to fight or kill any designated “enemy”. Modern male executives in the technology industry usually work in jeans, with little tie. In other working environments (e.g. insurance), this is a false dress. As a religious belief, in some regions female students may wear veils to attend classes, as this is necessary in certain cultures. When the Italians greet each other, they kiss on the cheeks in a fixed left-to-right order, while the Poles add another kiss. These expectations, social norms, determine the appropriate attitudes and behaviour in a given behavioural environment. Social norms can be broad guidelines, such as on what political or religious attitudes are considered acceptable. Social norms can also be very specific and can be reflected in standards of conduct, such as keeping shoes clean when the library is quiet or participating in job interviews. Social norms can even lead to dialogue, as they limit the discussion of sensitive or taboo topics in the face of certain groups, such as heterosexuals or groups with known political differences.

p27.original: 学习和适应社会规范 在各种情境下，有些规范是不成文的规则。例如，当老师讲课时，学生应该听讲而不是交谈。但是，如何规范你在电梯中的行为呢？我们打赌你总是面朝电梯门，在电梯里还有其他人的时候，你要么停止与朋友聊天，要么低声聊天。为什么？这些规则写在哪里？你是如何学习它们的？如果下次你进入一个载满人的电梯时，你面朝后方会发生什么？尝试一下这个小实验，看看其他人的反应是什么。这是20世纪60年代电视上的《快拍相机》（Candid Camera）节目中首次展示的经典实验“面朝后方”（Face the Rear）。或者当国歌响起每个人都站起来时，你尝试坐下来。要想了解某项社会规范是否正在发挥作用，只需尝试违反它，并检查在同一环境中其他人的反应。如果他们表现出困惑，你就会知道自己违反了规范，然后准备受到一些抨击吧。
p27.en: Learning and adapting to social norms, some of them are unwritten rules in various contexts. For example, when teaching, students should listen rather than talk. But how do you regulate your behaviour in the elevator? We bet you're always facing the elevator door, and when there's someone else in the elevator, you stop talking to your friends or you're whispering. Why? Where are these rules written? How do you learn them? What happens next when you get into a crowded elevator, you face back? Try this little experiment and see what the rest of you are responding to. This is the first classic experiment on TV in the 1960s, "Face the Real." Or when the national anthem rings everyone up, you try to sit down. To understand whether a social norm is working, it is necessary to try to violate it and to check the reactions of others in the same environment. If they show confusion, you will know that you have violated the norm and will be ready to be attacked.

p28.original: 当一个人加入一个新团体时，如工作小组或一群朋友，会有一个调整期。在此期间，个人会试图找到融入这个团体的最佳方式。融入团体通常需要发现其社会规范。在做出这种调整时，个人通过两种方式：首先其注意到某些行为的一致性和规律性，然后观察他人违反社会规范时的负面后果。
p28.en: When a person joins a new group, such as working groups or a group of friends, there is a period of adjustment. During this period, individuals will try to find the best way to integrate into the group. Integration groups usually need to find their social norms. In making such adjustments, the individual takes two forms: first, he takes note of the consistency and regularity of certain acts and then looks at the negative consequences of the violation of social norms by others.

p29.original: 例如，如果一个新学生刚进入你的学校就读，他常使用公文包携带书本和笔记本，而校内的其他学生习惯使用双肩包，那么他的行为就会被视为“怪异”。在其他学校也是这样。虽然很少被明确提出，但是着装要求也是如此，它几乎可以影响每个人的着装（见图11-2）。在上一代人的观念中，侧戴棒球帽的家伙会被嘲笑，穿着破牛仔裤的妇女可能会被认为太穷了，没钱购买新牛仔裤，如今却是一种流行的穿戴。现在，运动员佩戴钻石耳环或身上有大面积文身也逐渐流行。此外，一些人已经使用简洁握手方式取代了“老式的”繁复的握手仪式。
p29.en: For example, if a new student has just entered your school and he often uses briefcases to carry books and notebooks, while other students in the school are accustomed to using double shoulder bags, his behaviour is considered to be “wrong”. The same is true in other schools. Although rarely explicitly stated, the same is true of dress requirements, which can affect almost everyone's dress (see figure 11-2). In the view of the previous generation, men wearing baseball caps were ridiculed, and women in rags might be considered too poor to have the money to buy new jeans, which is now a popular dress. The wearing of diamond earrings or the presence of large areas of tattoos by athletes is now becoming more prevalent. In addition, some have replaced “old” and complex handshakes with a simple handshake.

p30.original: 图11-2 社会规范随时间而变化

p33.original: 想一下你在特定情境中违反社会规范的时刻。你是故意还是无意识地违反它的？你和别人的感受如何？
p33.en: Think of the moment when you break social norms in a given situation. Did you deliberately or unconsciously violate it? How are you feeling with someone else?

p35.original: 为了帮助我们组织所有的信息并更好地指导我们的行动，我们形成了图式（schemas）。形成图式后，我们能够对各种情境下人们期望的事物做出预测。因此，当我们违反图式时，常常会因为无法进行预测而感到不安。想象一下，当你进入一家（非快餐店）餐馆，开始点餐，还未上菜就收到账单。想象服务员先上甜点，然后是主菜，最后是开胃菜。这完全在意料之外！图式是指人们在某些情境下应该做出的行为。当他们不这样做时，会引起负面的效果，因为我们认为他人的行为必须符合我们的图式。餐馆的例子就与违反事件发生的图式相关。
p35.en: In order to help us organize all the information and better guide our actions, we have developed the map (schemas). With this pattern, we can predict what people expect in all circumstances. As a result, when we violate the pattern, we are often disturbed by the inability to predict. Imagine, when you get into a restaurant, start ordering, you get bills before you eat. Imagine the waiter taking dessert, then the main course, and finally the appetizer. This is completely unexpected! The diagram refers to the behaviour that people are supposed to perform in certain circumstances. When they do not do so, it can have negative effects, because we believe that the behaviour of others must be in line with our pattern. The example of restaurants is linked to the pattern of violations.

p36.original: 脚本（script）是一个人对事件和行为动作序列的知识，是在特定情境下对特定社会角色的期望。我们期待事件的进程是以标准的、可预测的顺序发生的。
p36.en: Scripts (scripts) are a person's knowledge of the sequence of events and behaviour and are an expectation of a particular social role in a given situation. We expect that the process of events will take place in a standard and predictable sequence.

p37.original: 11.1.3 社会规范影响学生的政治观点
p37.en: 11.1.3 Social norms influence students ' political views

p38.original: 我们知道父母会影响孩子的政治观点，但是学生的政治观点会受教师的政治观点影响吗？社会心理学家西奥多·纽科姆（Theodore Newcomb）提出了这个问题。
p38.en: We know that parents influence the political views of children, but are students' political views influenced by the political views of teachers? The Social Psychologist Theodore Newcomb raised the issue.

p39.original: 1. 学院：佛蒙特州（Vermont）的本宁顿学院（Bennington College）。

p40.original: 2. 时间：20世纪30年代，是有争议的总统富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福（Franklin Delano Roosevelt）时代。
p40.en: 2. Timing: The 1930s were the era of controversial President Franklin Delano Roosevelt.

p41.original: 3. 学生：来自富裕、保守家庭的女生，她们的价值观绝对保守。
p41.en: 3. Students: Girls from wealthy, conservative families whose values are absolutely conservative.

p42.original: 4. 师资力量：年轻、充满活力、自由。
p42.en: 4. Teacher strength: young, dynamic and free.

p43.original: 当时，本宁顿的校园文化规范是政治和经济自由主义。研究人员想知道：家庭和教师中的哪一个最能影响这些学生的态度？你的预测是什么？显然，任何预测都会使当时的情境力量（教师）与长期且非情境的力量（家庭）相对。但出乎意料的是，实验数据显示，短期的校园规范比长期的家庭规范的影响力更大。大多数女生的保守主义态度随着她们的大学生活而发生了变化，在大四时，她们的思想和逻辑思维明显已经转变为自由主义式的（Newcomb，1943）。但是，这种态度转变是否会长久地持续下去？
p43.en: At that time, the campus cultural norm in Bennington was political and economic liberalism. Researchers would like to know which of the families and teachers is best placed to influence the attitudes of these students. What's your prediction? Clearly, any predictions will compare the then situational forces (teachers) to the longer-term and non-temporal forces (family). However, it is unexpected that experimental data show that short-term school norms are more influential than long-term family norms. The conservative attitude of the majority of girls has changed with their university life, and in their fourth year, their thinking and logic had clearly been transformed into liberal (Newcomb, 1943). But will this change of attitude be sustained in the long term?

p44.original: 的确是这样。毕业时是自由主义者的女生之后仍然是自由主义者。反对现行的自由主义规范的少数人之后仍然是保守的。这种情况可以部分归因于她们都嫁给了与自己的政治态度类似的人。
p44.en: Indeed. After graduating as a liberal girl, she was still a liberal. The minority who opposes the current liberal norms remains conservative. This is partly due to the fact that they are married to people who have similar political attitudes.

p45.original: 无论这些女生是自由派还是保守派，大多数人都嫁给了政治态度与自己类似的人，从而营造了支持性的新家庭环境，以维持这些不同的意识形态。在大约30年后的1960年美国总统大选中，这些妇女仍然保持当时在本宁顿学院形成的自由主义，当时纽科姆调查的班级有60%的人投票支持自由民主党人约翰·肯尼迪（John Kennedy），而不是保守的共和党人理查德·尼克松（Richard Nixon），相比之下，同一时期其他大学的毕业生对肯尼迪的支持率不足30%（Newcomb et al.，1967）。
p45.en: Whether these girls are liberal or conservative, most of them marry people with similar political attitudes to themselves, thus creating a supportive new family environment to sustain these different ideologies. In the 1960 United States presidential election, some 30 years later, these women continued to be liberals that were formed at Bennington College when 60 per cent of the classes in the Newcom survey voted for the Free Democrat John Kennedy instead of the conservative Republican Richard Nixon, compared to less than 30 per cent of the backers of other universities during the same period (Newcomb et al., 1967).

p46.original: 如表11-1所示，在本宁顿学院最初发现的趋势仍存在于当今的学生中。学生这一群体在上大学时的态度会变得更加自由。虽然不是全部，但大多数人都会如此。保守派专家经常把这种趋势归咎于自由派教授的灌输。但数据表明，同龄人对大学生观点的影响要大于教师对大学生的影响。
p46.en: As shown in Table 11-1, the initial trends observed at Bennington College remain among current students. The student group is more liberal when entering university. Not all of them, but most of them do. Conservative experts often attributed this trend to the indoctrination of liberal professors. However, the data show that the influence of peers on university views is greater than that of teachers on university students.

p47.original: 表11-1 美国大学生的政治价值观
p47.en: Table 11-1 Political values of American university students

p48.original: ①这些数字仅从具有 TFS 和 CSS 数据的案例中编制而成（N=12205）。
p48.en: 1 These figures are based only on cases where TFS and CSS data are available (N=1205).

p49.original: 注：数据表明，在大多数情境下，21世纪的学生（就像本宁顿学院的20世纪30年代的学生一样）在读大学期间其政治价值观变得更加进步。
p49.en: Note: The data show that in most cases, students of the 21st century (as in the 1930s at Bennington College) have become more advanced in their political values during their university studies.

p50.original: 当然，群体规范和群体压力并不是校园文化的唯一来源。一个人的工作场所、邻里、宗教团体和家庭，都会传达行为标准和违反这些规范的制裁措施（如开除、遭到社会排斥或逐出教会）。但是高中或大学的环境可能会对年轻人产生巨大影响。如果他们的生活经验有限并且以前从未遇到过与自己的态度截然不同的情境，则尤其如此。例如，在本宁顿研究中，新生通常会接受同学们的政治观点，并经常认同同学们的宗教信仰及对性和酒精的态度（Prentice & Miller，1993；Schroeder & Prentice，1995）。而对于住在宿舍、与舍友一起吃饭和进行课后活动的住校学生，社会规范对这些学生的行为产生的影响甚至比走读学生更加明显。
p50.en: Of course, group norms and group pressure are not the only sources of school culture. A person's workplace, neighbourhood, religious group and family communicates standards of conduct and sanctions for violations of these norms (e.g. expulsion, social exclusion or expulsion from church). However, the high school or university environment may have a significant impact on young people. This is particularly true if they have limited experience in their lives and have never experienced a situation that is different from their own attitudes before. For example, in the Bennington study, freshmen usually accept the political views of their fellow students and often share their religious beliefs and attitudes towards sex and alcohol (Printice & Miller, 1993); Schroeder & Prentice, 1995. For students living in dormitories, eating with their roommates and carrying out after-school activities, the social norms have had even more significant effects on the behaviour of these students than on those who go to school.

p53.original: 评价影响从众和不从众的因素。
p53.en: The factors affecting both the public and the private sector are evaluated.

p54.original: 社会压力的力量有多强呢？有研究表明社会压力对人们的情绪、着装风格和休闲活动都会产生影响（Totterdell，2000；Totterdell et al.，1998）。这种模仿他人的倾向被称为变色龙效应（chameleon effect）。变色龙这种动物会通过改变肤色，使自己融入不同的环境（Chartrand & Bargh，1999）。在上文中，我们已经了解到社会压力对本宁顿学院学生政治态度的影响。
p54.en: How powerful is the pressure of society? Research shows that social pressures affect people's emotions, dress styles and leisure activities (Totterdell, 2000); Totterdell et al., 1998). This tendency to imitate others is called chameleon effect. An animal such as Chameleons can integrate itself into different environments by changing colour (Chartrand & Bargh, 1999). As mentioned above, we have learned about the impact of social pressures on the political attitudes of students at the Bennington College.

p55.original: 但是，社会影响力是否足以使人们遵循明显错误的群体规范？
p55.en: But are social influences sufficient to enable people to follow clearly erroneous group norms?

p56.original: 这种情境的力量比你亲眼所见的证据更有力吗？
p56.en: Are these situations more powerful than the evidence you see?

p57.original: 一群陌生人能让你通过他们错误的感知来了解世界吗？
p57.en: Can a bunch of strangers let you understand the world through their misperceptions?

p59.original: 11.2.1 阿希效应：处于多数派中的少数派
p59.en: 11.2.1 Ash effect: minorities in the majority

p60.original: 一位接待员将最后到达的被试带进等待室。当这名被试与其他六名被试交谈时了解到，大家参与的是同一个实验。但最后到达的这名被试不知道其他六个人是实验者的同谋——在社会心理学研究中通常被称为“联盟”（confederates）。他们对精心安排的计划进行了排练，要对真正的实验被试施加社会压力。
p60.en: A receptionist took the last person to the waiting room. When the person was tried and interviewed with six other persons, it became clear that you were involved in the same experiment. But the last person who arrived was not aware that the other six were accomplices of the experiment — commonly referred to as “coalitions” in sociopsychological studies. They rehearsed well-arranged plans and put social pressure on real experiments.

p61.original: 不久，实验者进入等待室并邀请所有被试进入另一个房间，他们坐在一排椅子上，椅子对面有一个画架。在画架上，他们看到一叠大卡片，如图11-3右侧所示，卡片上有四条竖线。
p61.en: Shortly afterwards, the experimenters entered the waiting room and invited all of them to be tested in another room, sitting in a row of chairs opposite which had a drawing shelf. On the frame, they saw a large pile of cards with four vertical lines, as shown on the right side of figure 11-3.

p62.original: 任务内容是判断A、B、C三条线的哪一条与标准线X的长度相同。实验者开始随意地收集被试给出的判断，收集顺序是从假被试开始。每个人都觉得这个简单的任务有点无聊。
p62.en: The task is to determine which of the A, B and C lines is the same length as standard X. The experimenter began to collect the test judgement at random, starting with the false test. Everyone thinks this simple task is a bit boring.

p63.original: 一切都进展顺利，直到呈现第三张卡片。卡片如图11-3所示，正确答案显然是B，所以不知情的真被试对第一个人说“A”的情况感到难以置信。作为一名心理学学生，真被试知道不同的人对世界的感知觉不同，所以他简单地将这种反应归因于个体知觉偏差。之后第二个人也回答“A”。当第三和第四个人也说“A”时，真被试开始怀疑，“我的感知觉是否出现了偏差？”作为倒数第二个被试，他的看法与之前五个人的判断相冲突。他再次看了看卡片，结结巴巴地说：“嗯……A。”最后一个被试也选择A。
p63.en: Everything went well until the third card was presented. The correct answer to the card, as shown in figure 11-3, is clearly B, so the uninformed truth is incredibly hard to believe when the first person says “A”. As a student of psychology, it was true that different people felt different about the world, so he simply attributed that reaction to individual perception deviations. The second person then answered “A”. When the third and fourth people also said “A”, it really began to wonder, “Do I have a deviation in my senses? “As the penultimate trial, his view conflicted with the judgement of the five preceding. He looked at the card again and stammered and said, "Well, a." The last one was tried and also selected A.

p64.original: 实验总共包括18张卡片，其他被试有时给出“正确”的答案，但他们在12个试次中做出了明显错误的判断。他们疯了吗？震惊之余，真被试继续附和着他人的“错误”，并且认为此时自己提出异议会破坏实验，采取这个行为是不合适的。
p64.en: The experiment consisted of a total of 18 cards, and others were given “right” answers at times, but they made a clear miscalculation in 12 of them. Are they crazy? It was not appropriate to continue to be appalled by the “mistakes” of others and to consider that their own objections at this time would undermine the experiment.

p65.original: 在这种情况下你会怎么做？
p65.en: What would you do in such a situation?

p66.original: 你可能会认为，如果自己真的参加了阿希的实验，会抵抗住这种压力。或许可以，事实上，在阿希最初的实验中，近三分之二的真被试经受住了群体的压力，不去附和明显错误的判断。但是，重要的是，有三分之一的学生从众，这意味着他们由于社会压力而违背了自己的感知觉。
p66.en: You might think that if you actually took part in Ash's experiment, you'd resist the pressure. Perhaps, indeed, in Ash's initial experiment, almost two thirds of the true population was tried to withstand the pressure of the group and did not go along with a manifestly erroneous judgement. However, what is important is that one third of the students are from the public, which means that they are being held against their senses because of social pressure.

p67.original: 社会心理学家将这种现象称为阿希效应（asch effect）：一个群体对个体客观判断施加的强大影响。所罗门·阿希（Solomon Asch）的实验已经成为从众（conformity）的经典例证，即人们具有采纳其他群体成员的行为和观点的倾向。尽管个体是在评判客观存在的事实，而不是发表个人的意见，但许多人还是会屈服于从众的压力。
p67.en: Social psychologists refer to this phenomenon as the Ashch effect: the powerful influence of a group on an individual's objective judgement. The experiment of Solomon Asch has become a classic example of the tendency of people to adopt the behaviour and views of members of other groups. Although individuals are judging objective facts rather than expressing their views, many are subject to pressure from the public.

p68.original: 图11-3 阿希的从众实验

p69.original: 注：该图片来自阿希开创性的研究，右图是典型的刺激阵列。左图显示12个试次的从众结果，图中显示了大多数假被试给出错误的答案（底部的线）或真被试有一个持有异议的同伴（中间线）时的正确估计的百分比。
p69.en: Note: This picture is from the groundbreaking study of Ash, and the right picture is a typical stimulus array. The left figure shows the crowd results of 12 trials, showing the percentage of the correct estimate when most falsely given the wrong answer (line at the bottom) or actually tried to have a dissenting companion (middle line).

p70.original: 这一结果鼓励阿希和其他人对实验条件稍作调整，他们发现在某种情境下，三分之二的被试屈服于多数人。阿希和其他研究人员发现促进从众的条件有哪些呢？
p70.en: This result encouraged Ash and others to make minor adjustments to the conditions of the experiment, and they found that, in a certain situation, two thirds of them had been tried in favour of the majority. What are the conditions for the promotion of public opinion found by Ash and other researchers?

p71.original: 多数派的一致性。如果群体中的每个人都持相同的意见，他们可以产生强大的社会压力。但是，如果有一个人反对大多数人的意见，咒语就会被打破，从众的比例就急剧降低（Asch，1940，1955，1956）。
p71.en: Majority unity. If everyone in the group shares the same opinion, they can generate strong social pressure. However, if one person objects to the majority opinion, the spell will be broken and the proportion of the population will be drastically reduced (Asch, 1940, 1955, 1956).

p72.original: 群体的大小。在只有一两个人的群体中，大多数被试会明显感受到更少的从众压力。当被试面对的群体人数为三人及以上时，压力会骤增。
p72.en: Size of the group. In a group of only one or two people, most of them were tested to feel significantly less pressure from the crowd. When the number of groups tested is three or more, the pressure increases sharply.

p73.original: 进行公开判断，而不是私下判断。如果你相信群体中的其他人不会听到你的回答，那当你认为他们不正确时，你就不太可能附和他人（Deutsch & Gerard，1955）。
p73.en: Public rather than private. If you believe that the rest of the group will not hear your answer, it is unlikely that you will be able to associate with others when you think they are incorrect (Deutsch & Gerard, 1955).

p74.original: 模棱两可。当线段长度几乎相同，即正确的答案不是很清晰时，人们似乎更容易自我怀疑，并屈服于从众压力。
p74.en: Paradoxious. When the length of the line is almost the same, i.e. the correct answer is not clear, it seems that people are more susceptible to self-doubt and submit to pressure from the crowd.

p75.original: 自尊。如你猜想的一样，那些认为自我价值低的人更有可能在阿希实验中从众（Aronson，2011）。
p75.en: Self-esteem. As you imagine, those who think that they are of low self-worth are more likely to come from the Ash experiment (Aronson, 2011).

p76.original: 多数派的组合。与自尊的发现一致，当该群体的地位很高时（Eagly，1987），或者个人认为群体很重要时，个人更易从众。顺便说一句，除非该任务是通常针对男性的任务，如判断电器的质量（Eagly & Carli，1981），否则女性并不比男性更易从众。
p76.en: The majority group. Consistent with the discovery of self-esteem, individuals are more accessible when the group is of high standing (Eagly, 1987) or when the individual considers the group important. By the way, unless the task is usually directed at men, such as judging the quality of electrical appliances (Eagly & Carli, 1981), women are not much more visible than men.

p77.original: 独立性。虽然从众带来的压力很大，但少部分个体仍能够抵制它并保持自己的观点。他们甚至会在群体给出正确答案时故意给出错误的答案（Friend et al.，1990）。
p77.en: Independence. While the pressure from the crowd is high, a small number of individuals are able to resist it and maintain their own perspective. They even deliberately give the wrong answer when the group gives the right answer (Friend et al., 1990).

p78.original: 一致性中断。当群体中多数人的意见一致时，从众的概率最大。一旦一致意见被打破，从众的概率就会急剧下降（Allen & Levine，1969；Morris & Miller，1975）。
p78.en: Consistency is interrupted. When the majority of the population is in agreement, it is most likely to be from the outside. Once the consensus has been broken, the probability of a crowd is drastically reduced (Allen & Levine, 1969; Morris & Miller, 1975.

p79.original: 盟友的力量。我们想强调一个与个人有关的发现：哪怕只有一个盟友挑战群体标准，对你抵抗群体压力也是至关重要的。在一个很大的群体中，如果出现一个持异议的同盟者，会极大地降低从众性（见图11-3）。正是由于拥有了这样的“伙伴”，几乎所有的被试都抵制住了从众的压力。这项结果给了我们最积极的启示。如果你愿意公开挑战群体，那么你就可能影响其他人的行为。一个英雄就可以激励其他人不要屈服于群体压力。我们称其为“一人力量”。而“二人力量”是指当你忠于某人，或者由于某人在特定情境下的种族、宗教或性别地位而被欺负或抛弃时，与他成为盟友并反抗群体压力时产生的力量。
p79.en: Ally's power. We would like to highlight an individual-related discovery: even if only one ally challenges the standards of the group, it will be crucial for you to resist the pressure on the group. In one large group, the presence of a dissenting ally would greatly reduce the public profile (see figure 11-3). It is because of such a “partner” that almost all of them have been tried to resist the pressure from the outside. This result has given us the most positive inspiration. If you are willing to openly challenge the group, then you may affect the behaviour of others. One hero can inspire others not to yield to group pressure. We call it “one power”. The term “two power” refers to the power that arises when you are loyal to someone, or when you are bullied or abandoned because of a person's race, religion or gender status in a given situation, and you become an ally and resist group pressure.

p81.original: 所以现在想象一下，你即将在一个群体中公开投票，就像在俱乐部或董事会中常见的那样。在以下情景中，你有可能会从众：
p81.en: So imagine now that you're going to vote publicly in a group, as is common in clubs or boards. In the following scenarios, you may be in public:

p82.original: （1）正在解决复杂或令人困惑的问题；
p82.en: (1) Complex or confusing issues are being addressed;

p83.original: （2）小组中的其他人似乎了解他们所争论的问题；
p83.en: (2) The other members of the Panel appear to be aware of the issues at issue;

p84.en: (3) A public vote, not an anonymous vote;

p85.original: （4）整个群体在你之前投票，并且意见一致；
p85.en: (4) The whole group voted before you and agreed;

p87.original: 了解这种从众压力会让你更明智地进行思考：你如何面对群体中产生的从众问题，特别是在他们正朝着错误甚至不道德的方向发展的情境下。抵制这种影响需要批判性思维，并且还需要在此书中学到的知识，以及关于社会压力影响因素的知识。
p87.en: Understanding this kind of crowd pressure will make you think more wisely about how you confront the problems that arise among the groups, especially in situations where they are moving in the wrong or even immoral direction. Combating this impact requires critical thinking and learning from this book, as well as knowledge of the factors influencing social stress.

p89.original: 1. 人因规范性的影响而从众，并且希望被别人接受、认可和喜欢，而不是被他人排斥；
p89.en: 1. The human being is a person of public opinion because of his or her normative influence and wishes to be accepted, accepted and liked by others, rather than rejected by others;

p90.original: 2. 从众的另一个原因是信息影响，人们希望自己是正确的，并且了解在任何特定情境下正确的行为方式。
p90.en: 2. Another reason for this is the influence of information, the desire of people to be right and to understand the correct behaviour in any given situation.

p91.original: 当实验者的同谋对真被试撒谎时，这样的从众研究显然会带来伦理问题。但是，怎样才能确保使用阿希的基本范式时不发生欺骗？如果每个人都戴着眼镜看线条，真被试的眼镜是清晰的，所显示的线段和现实中的线段一样。但是大多数学生的护目镜被偷梁换柱了，虽然他们也能看到线段，结果却是扭曲的，不同长度的线段看起来和标准线段一样长。在一项研究中就使用了这种技术，被试戴的眼镜与带有偏振滤镜的3D电影中的眼镜相似（Mori & Arai，2010）。在这项研究中，104名日本学生被分成四组进行测试：其中三组戴着扭曲现实的眼镜，另一组戴着普通眼镜。结果显示，在没有欺骗的同谋情境下也产生了阿希的从众效应，并且女性被试中的从众概率高于阿希最初的研究数据。随后的一项调查性别差异的研究（Mori & Arai，2010）表明，在早年，日本文化中的男孩和女孩都会从众，但随着年龄的增长，男孩变得更加独立，女孩则保持不变。我们还需要进行其他研究，以确定从众的影响有多深远。
p91.en: Such an introspective study would obviously raise ethical questions when the experimenter's accomplices lied to the truth. But how can it be ensured that Ash's basic paradigm is used without deception? If everyone was looking at the lines with glasses, the real ones were clear, and the lines were shown in the same way as the ones in reality. However, most students have been replaced with goggles, and although they can also see lines, the results are distorted, with different lengths of lines as long as standard lines. This technique was used in one study, where the glasses tested were similar to those in the 3D film with an oscillation filter (Mori & Arai, 2010). In this study, 104 Japanese students were tested in four groups: three with distorted glasses and the other with ordinary glasses. The results also show that, in the absence of fraudulent complicity, there is an accelerator effect on Ash and that the probability of women being tested is higher than the initial research data on Ash. A subsequent study of gender differences (Mori & Arai, 2010) showed that boys and girls in Japanese culture were visible in the early years, but that girls remained the same as boys became more independent as they grew older. We also need other studies to determine how far-reaching the public impact is.

p92.en: 11.2.3 Rejected from the crowd or something.

p93.original: 什么时候最好依靠现有的社交信息？什么时候应该保持独立？你怎样认为？
p93.en: When do you think it's best to rely on existing social information? When should independence be maintained? What do you think?

p94.original: 即使对细菌理论不太了解，大多数人也遵循这个规则：在准备食物前或参加社交聚会后用肥皂洗手。在有许多行为选择的情境下，从众是很好的。支持这一结论的实验是最近一组关于不列颠哥伦比亚大学（University of British Columbia）学生的测试，以及与阿希的线段判断任务中被试类似的大众群体的实验（Muth ukrishna et al.，in press）。最有趣的发现是智商与反从众的关系。智商较高的人倾向于保持独立，他们比智商处于平均水平的人更多地拒绝从众。然而，当不确定性很高时，非常聪明的人会做出从众的策略反应。
p94.en: Even with little knowledge of bacterial theory, most people follow the rule of washing hands with soap before preparing food or after attending social gatherings. In situations where there are many behavioural choices, it is good to be from the public. The experiment in support of this conclusion was a recent set of tests of British Columbia University students and experiments with a similar mass group in the line-judgement mission with Ash (Muth ukrishna et al., in pres). The most interesting finding is the relationship between IQ and the anti-subsidiary. People with higher IQs tend to remain independent, and they are more open-minded than those with an IQ on average. However, when uncertainty is high, very smart people react in a tactical manner.

p96.original: 阿希的实验已经传入世界各地，大多数群体的结果显著相似。在阿希最初设定的实验条件下，不同社会中屈服于群体压力的比例大约是三分之一。表11-2显示了此类研究的一些典型结果。
p96.en: Ash's experiments have been brought into the world, and the results of most groups are significantly similar. Under the experimental conditions initially set by Ash, the proportion of different societies giving in to group pressure is about one third. Table 11-2 shows some of the typical results of such studies.

p97.original: 表11-2 阿希研究中的跨文化差异
p97.en: Table 11-2 Intercultural Differences in Archi Studies

p98.original: 这些一致性的结果表明，在不同文化中是同一种力量在起作用。然而，我们仍需警惕，这些调查的被试大多是大学生，他们在许多方面不同于社会中的其他人。一些研究发现，这些从众的结果也存在例外，这让我们对从众和文化之间的有趣关系进行一些思考。例如，在罗德西亚（现为津巴布韦）的班图文化中，51%的人有从众行为。解释这一结果很容易，因为在班图的文化中，对不符合社会习俗的行为通常处以重罚。还有一个例外，德国学生的从众百分比是22%。这么低的百分比令人惊讶。这可归因于德国样本的年龄，它比其他群体更大，但是更有可能是由于：人们从被纳粹领导的前几代德国人中吸取了教训，产生了更多的反从众行为。
p98.en: The results of these convergences show that the same forces work in different cultures. However, we still need to be vigilant, as most of these investigations have been conducted by university students, who are in many ways different from the rest of society. Some studies have found that there are exceptions to these public results, which have led us to reflect on interesting relationships between people and cultures. For example, 51 per cent of the Bantu culture in Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) has public behaviour. It is easy to interpret this result, as in Bantu culture, serious penalties are usually imposed for behaviour that is not in accordance with social custom. An exception is the fact that the percentage of students in Germany is 22 per cent. That's an amazingly low percentage. This can be attributed to the age of the German sample, which is larger than the rest of the population, but is more likely to be due to the fact that people have learned from previous generations of Nazi-led Germans, which have produced more anti-optimal behaviour.

p99.original: 然而，最令人惊讶的结果可能是日本学生中不从众的百分比很高。一般人通常认为日本人会服从群体规范。然而，在阿希的实验中，日本被试从众的百分比非常低，仅为25%，甚至明显低于看似不喜欢从众的美国人。此外，日本被试的反从众率尤其高，即故意排斥群体规范：34%的人在小组其他成员给出正确答案时故意给出错误答案！一个可能的原因是，日本的服从文化并非处处存在，人们只是在其乐意效忠的群体中才会做出服从行为。因此，当日本学生面对一群陌生人做出判断时，他们几乎感受不到从众的压力，因为他们不属于这个群体。
p99.en: The most surprising result, however, is probably a high percentage of students in Japan who are not in the public domain. It is generally believed that Japanese will be subject to group norms. However, in Ash's experiment, Japan's percentage of people tried out was very low, at 25 per cent, and even significantly lower than the apparently unpopular American population. In addition, Japan has been tested against a particularly high level of opposition, i.e. the deliberate rejection of group norms: 34 per cent of the people deliberately gave the wrong answer when the other members of the Panel gave the right answer! One possible reason is that Japan's culture of obedience does not exist everywhere, and that people only behave in a group of people they are willing to serve. Thus, when Japanese students judge against a group of strangers, they hardly feel the pressure from the outside, because they do not belong to this group.

p101.original: 土耳其裔美国心理学家穆扎费尔·谢里夫（Muzafer Sherif，1935）曾做过一项经典实验，证明了社会影响如何使行为规范内化。被试被要求判断一个静止光点的移动距离，由于这一光点完全在黑暗中，没有参照点，所以它看起来似乎在移动。我们称这种感知错觉为游动效应（autokinetic effect）。最初，同一被试的判断结果差异很大。然而，当这个被试与其他陌生被试组成一个群体，并被要求大声报告他们的判断时，他们的判断开始趋同。他们看到光线朝着同一方向移动，并且移动的距离也相似。更有趣的是谢里夫研究的最后一部分——当被试在此之后独自待在同一个昏暗的房间里再次观察时，他们继续遵循在群体中形成的规范。这与阿希的研究类似，群体影响了个体知觉。
p101.en: Muzafer Sherif, 1935, a Turkish-American psychologist, had done a classic experiment that demonstrated how social influence internalized behavioural norms. It was tried to determine the distance of movement of a static light point, which appeared to be moving because it was completely dark and had no reference point. We call this sensory illusion a locomotive effect. Initially, the same trial findings varied widely. However, when this alien has been tried to form a group and has been asked to report their judgement aloud, their judgement has begun to converge. They saw the light moving in the same direction and the same distance. More interesting is the last part of the Sharif study — they continue to follow the norms that have been formed in the group when they are tried to be alone in a dark room again. This is similar to Ash's study, where groups affect individual consciousness.

p102.original: 此外，群体规范一旦形成，便会一直持续下去。通过进一步的研究，当对参加过游动效应实验的被试再次进行单独测试时，虽然没有前群体的成员目击他们的判断，但他们仍遵守当初形成的群体规范，甚至在一年之后也是如此（Rohrer et al.，1954）。这是证明社会信息影响力的有力证据。规范可以代代相传，即使创建规范的原始群体不存在了，它仍能影响人们的行为（Insko et al.，1980）。我们如何知道群体规范的这种跨代影响呢？在游动效应研究中，研究人员在每次实验后都会用一个新被试替换一个旧被试，直到小组所有被试都被更替成新的被试，在此过程中，群体的游动效应仍然起作用（Jacobs & Campbell，1961）。
p102.en: Moreover, group norms, once they are formed, will continue. Through further research, when the trial of participants in the vagabond effects was tested separately again, members of the former group, although not witnesses to their judgement, complied with the norms of the group that had been formed, even one year later (Rohrer et al., 1954). This is a strong evidence of the impact of social information. Norms can be transmitted from generation to generation, and even if the original group that created them does not exist, it can influence people's behaviour (Insko et al., 1980). How do we know this cross-generational impact of group norms? In the case of the motion effects study, researchers replace an old test with a new test after each experiment, until all the team's tests are replaced by a new test, in which the group's motion effects still work (Jacobs & Campbell, 1961).

p103.original: 从这个实验中，你能观察到现实生活中的规范是如何在企业、社区、城市、家庭或政治团体中代代相传的过程吗？这种规范成为文化的一部分，并决定了成员们应该如何以共同的方式看待世界。有时它能带来正面影响，例如，像苹果和谷歌这样的公司；但有时它却会导致很糟糕的问题，例如，腐败的安然公司和安达信会计事务所。正如我们所看到的，社会规范对我们的行为施加了强大且难以抗拒的影响。我们建议你观看2011年的纪录片《监守自盗》（Inside Job），以了解导致华尔街和全球金融危机的一些社会心理力量。我们强烈推荐的另一部电影是由奥斯卡获奖导演亚历克斯·吉布尼（Alex Gibney）执导的影片：《安然：房间里最聪明的人》（Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room）。
p103.en: From this experiment, can you see how the norms of real life are transmitted from generation to generation in enterprises, communities, cities, families or political groups? Such norms become part of culture and determine how members should view the world in a common way. Sometimes it has a positive impact, for example, on companies such as apples and Google; Sometimes, however, it can lead to very bad problems, such as corrupt Enron and Andersen accounting firms. As we have seen, social norms have had a powerful and irresistible impact on our behaviour. We suggest that you watch the 2011 documentary Inside Job to understand some of the psychosocial forces that led to Wall Street and the global financial crisis. Another film that we strongly recommend is directed by Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney: Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room.

p104.original: 11.2.6 从众和独立会激活不同的大脑脑区
p104.en: 11.2.6 Different brain regions are activated from the public and independent.

p105.original: 如今，在阿希时代未开发出的新技术为我们提供了一些关于从众的有趣见解，它展示了在从众过程中大脑活动所扮演的角色。当人们出现从众行为时，是出于规范的需要而理性地决定与群体合作，还是他们的感知觉真的发生了改变，误判了群体提供的错误信息的有效性？一项使用先进的脑部扫描技术的研究（Berns et al.，2005）回答了这个问题。它还回答了阿希效应能否适用于当代更有经验的学生。我们可以提前知道答案为“适用”。
p105.en: Today, new technologies that were not launched during the time of Ash offer us some interesting insights about the public, which demonstrate the role played by brain activity in the process. Is it true that when people behave from the public, they decide rationally to work with groups because of the need for norms, or do their perceptions really change, misjudge the validity of erroneous information provided by groups? A study using advanced brain scanning techniques (Berns et al., 2005) answered this question. It also answered whether the Ash effect could be applied to more experienced students in the contemporary era. We could have known in advance that the answer was “applied”.

p106.original: 现如今通过使用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI），当被试进行各种任务时，研究人员可以检测到变得活跃的大脑，并且可以检测到当一个人执行特定的实验任务时哪些特定的大脑区域会变得活跃。通过了解每个大脑区域控制的心理功能的不同，我们可以知道特定的实验任务激活的某个脑区究竟意味着什么。
p106.en: Now, by using functional MRI images, researchers can detect the brain that becomes active when they are tested for various tasks and can detect specific brain areas that become active when a person performs a specific experimental mission. By understanding the different psychological functions of each brain area, we can see what a particular brain region is actually meant by a given experimental mission.

p107.original: 下面是研究的过程。想象一下，你是被招募来参加知觉实验的32名被试之一。你必须对三维物体的图像进行心理旋转，并判断它与标准物体是否相同。在等待室里，你遇到了另外4个被试，你开始和他们一起玩电脑游戏、互相拍照、聊天。他们的真实身份是演员，是实验者的“同盟”，他们很快就会在实验中编造一致的答案，但与你给出的正确答案不一致。你会被选中进行大脑扫描，而其他人以组为单位在外面观察图像，并讨论它们是否相同。其余的步骤遵循阿希的原始实验，演员们会给出错误的答案，而你必须决定是从众还是绝不动摇。
p107.en: The process of research follows. Imagine you're one of the 32 people who was recruited to participate in the sensory experiment. You have to rotate images of 3D objects psychologically and judge whether they are identical to standard objects. In the waiting room, you met four other people who were tested, and you started playing computer games with them, taking pictures of each other, talking. Their true identities are actors, the “allies” of the experimenters, who soon will invent consistent answers in the experiment, but they are not in line with the correct answers you gave. You'll be selected for brain scanning, while others will observe the images outside in groups and discuss whether they're the same. The remaining steps follow Ash's original experiment, and actors give the wrong answer, and you have to decide whether to be from the crowd or not to waver.

p108.original: 结果如何？与阿希的实验一样，真被试屈服于群体压力，在41%的情况下会给出同其他人一样的错误答案。在屈服于群体的错误判断时，大脑扫描结果显示，从众时会使负责视觉和空间感知的大脑皮层（具体来说是右顶内沟）的活动增加。令人惊讶的是，负责监控冲突、计划和其他更高层次心理活动的前脑中的一些脑区活动没有发生变化。那些做出独立判断与群体对抗的人，在与情感显著相关的脑区，即右侧杏仁核（amygdala）及相关脑区产生了额外的活动。这意味着抗拒给那些保持独立的人造成了情感上的负担，也就是因自主性而付出了心理代价。
p108.en: How'd it go? Like Ash's experiment, it was really submissive to group pressure, giving the wrong answer in 41 per cent of cases, like the others. In giving in to the wrong judgement of the group, brain scans show that the activity of the brain cortex (specifically, the right-top gutter) responsible for visual and spatial perception increases from time to time. Surprisingly, there has been no change in some of the brain regions in the front brain responsible for monitoring conflicts, plans and other higher levels of psychological activity. Those who make independent judgements and confront groups have generated additional activity in the emotionally significant brain region, i.e., the amygdala on the right, and the associated brain region. This means that resistance imposes an emotional burden on those who maintain their independence, that is, psychological costs for autonomy.

p109.original: 该研究的主要作者，神经科学家格雷戈里·伯恩斯和他的同事（Gregory Berns et al.，2005）总结道：“我们常常以为眼见为实，但研究表明，群体的观念才是真实的。”这意味着当别人的观点成为群体共识时，我们对外部世界重要方面的感知会受到影响，让人不禁质疑真理的本质。
p109.en: The leading author of the study, Gregory Berns et al., concluded with his colleague: “We often see what we see, but research shows that the idea of a group is real. “This means that when others' views become a group consensus, our perception of the important aspects of the outside world is affected and leaves the very essence of the truth in question.

p111.original: 我们只有认识到在社会压力下的脆弱性，才会在从众不符合我们的最大利益时开始对其进行反抗。问题是，许多人仍细想自己可以抵制从众，即“不是我”综合征。他们假设其他人可能会受到情境力量的影响，但是他们自己是可以抵抗这种力量的一类特殊人群。自相矛盾的是，这种天真的观点使他们更容易受到影响，因为他们的警惕性降低了，同时也没有对作用在他们身上的情境的影响力进行认真的、批判性的分析。因此，请记住，世界很多地方都有混蛋、阴谋家和腐败的人，他们知道如何让别人消费、投资或签署某种东西从而达成自己的目的，尤其是对那些天真的、盲信的人们，或者没有学会在思想上抵制、容易从众的天然脆弱性的人们来说，更要小心。
p111.en: We will only begin to fight society when we recognize its vulnerability under social pressure when it is not in our best interests. The problem is that many people still think that they can resist the public, that is, “not me”. They assume that others may be affected by situational forces, but they themselves are a special group of people who can resist such forces. Paradoxically, this naive view makes them more vulnerable because their vigilance is diminished and there is no serious and critical analysis of the impact of the situation on them. Therefore, remember that in many parts of the world there are assholes, conspirators and corrupt people who know how to let others consume, invest or sign something to achieve their own ends, especially those who are naive, blind, or who do not learn to resist intellectually and who are vulnerable to natural vulnerabilities.

p112.original: 值得一提的是，使用神经生物学技术研究社会心理过程正在社会心理学领域广泛开展，被称为社会神经科学（social neuroscience）。社会神经科学是一个跨学科领域，致力于了解生物系统如何实现社会过程和行为，并利用生物学概念和方法阐述和改进社会过程和行为的理论。在这个相对较新的领域中，研究人员正在使用完善的方法为传统的偏见、态度、自我控制和情绪调节带来新的理解（Azar，2002a；Cacioppo & Brentson，2005；Decety & Cacioppo，2011；Harmon-Jones & Winkielman，2007）。
p112.en: It is worth mentioning that the psycho-social process of studying using neurobiology techniques is being carried out extensively in the area of socio-psychology, known as social neuroscience. Social neuroscience is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to understand how biological systems achieve social processes and behaviour and to develop and improve the theory of social processes and behaviour using biological concepts and methods. In this relatively new field, researchers are using well-developed methods to bring new understandings to traditional prejudices, attitudes, self-control and emotional reconciliation (Azar, 2002a); Cacioppo & Brentson, 2005; Decety & Cacioppo, 2011; Harmon-Jones & Winkielman, 2007.

p113.original: 11.2.8 幼儿会从众，而猿类不会
p113.en: 11.2.8 Young children will be in the public domain, and apes will not.

p114.original: 为了发现年幼的儿童和猿类是否也会表现出对规范的从众，丹尼尔·豪恩（Daniel Haun）和他的研究小组对18个两岁儿童、12只黑猩猩和12只猩猩进行了一个基于奖励的实验。他们向每个被试都展示了一个盒子，盒子有三个分开的彩色区域，每个区域顶部都有一个孔。被试通过互动了解到，虽然可以将球放在三个区域中的任何一个，但只有一个区域可以提供奖励（猩猩的奖励是花生，儿童的奖励是巧克力）。在熟悉了盒子之后，被试随后观察到三个他们熟悉的同龄人在放置球时，都训练有素地选择了与自己喜好不同的同一个颜色区域。然后桌子转了过来，被试必须在同龄人的注视下决定将自己的球放到哪个区域。结果显示，与猩猩相比，儿童更可能调整其行为以使其与同龄人相匹配，尤其当同龄人在场时。虽然儿童有一半以上的时间遵循了相同的策略，但猩猩几乎忽略了它们的同龄人，坚持它们已学会的原始策略（Haun et al.，2014）。
p114.en: In order to discover whether young children and apes would also show a commitment to norms, Daniel Haun and his research team conducted an award-based experiment on 18 two-year-olds, 12 chimpanzees and 12 apes. They showed each of them a box with three separate coloured areas with a hole at the top of each area. It was tested through interaction that while the ball could be placed in either of the three regions, only one region could provide an incentive (the reward for gorillas is peanuts and the reward for children is chocolate). After familiarizing themselves with the box, three of their familiar peers were then observed with training to select the same colour area as their preferences. The table then turned around and was tried to decide which area to put its ball in with the eyes of its peers. The results show that children are more likely than apes to adapt their behaviour to match their peers, especially when they are present. Although more than half of the time children have followed the same strategy, gorillas almost ignore their peers and insist on the original strategies they have learned (Haun et al., 2014).

p116.original: 群体本身也可能会因压力而选择从众。群体思维是重要的社会心理过程术语，它促使个人在群体（如委员会）中进行思考和决策时保持一致。心理学家欧文·贾尼斯（Irving Janis，1972；Janis & Mann，1977）首次提出，在群体中，群体成员试图使他们的观点与群体达成共识的现象被称为群体思维（groupthink）。这种从众偏差会导致群体采取不明智的行为。
p116.en: The group itself may also be subject to pressure to choose its own audience. Group thinking is an important term for psychosocial processes, and it promotes consistency in individual thinking and decision-making within groups (e.g. committees). Psychologist Irving Janis, 1972; Janis & Mann, 1977, for the first time, suggested that within a group, members of the group tried to reach a consensus between their views and the group, known as group thinking (groupthink). Such deviations can lead to unwise behaviour by groups.

p117.original: 可能促进群体思维的五种情况：
p117.en: Five scenarios that may contribute to group thinking:

p118.original: 命令性的领导，一位占主导地位的领导者；

p119.original: 较高的团队凝聚力（cohesiveness），并且成员毫无异议；
p119.en: High team cohesion, with no objection from members;

p120.original: 缺乏对条理性地收集证据或评估程序的规范性要求；
p120.en: Lack of normative requirements for a rational collection of evidence or assessment procedures;

p121.original: 成员的社会背景和意识形态的同质性；
p121.en: The homogeneity of the social background and ideology of the members;

p122.original: 外部威胁带来的高压力，且找到优于群体负责人提出的解决方案的希望渺茫。
p122.en: The external threat is under high pressure and there is little hope of finding solutions better than those proposed by the group leaders.

p123.original: 这个概念最初是为了解释美国政府的错误决策，如珍珠港事件，尤其是1961年灾难性地入侵古巴猪湾事件。在该事件中，基于反卡斯特罗的古巴难民的错误报告，约翰·肯尼迪总统内阁的高级参谋做出了愚蠢的决定，入侵了古巴。后来，其他人将群体思维视为导致空难的错误决定和安然公司破产的影响因素。2003年布什政府决定对伊拉克发动战争，也是基于布什内阁中一些精明顾问的错误信念。他们相信萨达姆·侯赛因拥有核武器，并会将其运送给本·拉登，用于对美国发动另一场恐怖袭击（Schwartz & Wald，2003）。
p123.en: This concept was originally intended to explain the erroneous decisions of the United States Government, such as the Pearl Harbor incident, and in particular the catastrophic invasion of the Bay of Pigs in Cuba in 1961. In that incident, the senior staff of the Cabinet of President John F. Kennedy took a foolish decision to invade Cuba, based on false reports of anti-Castro Cuban refugees. Later, others saw group thinking as the wrong decision that led to the crash and the influence of Enron’s bankruptcy. The decision of the Bush Administration in 2003 to launch a war against Iraq was also based on the false belief of some of the wise advisers in the Bush Administration. They believed Saddam Hussein possessed nuclear weapons and would deliver them to bin Laden for another terrorist attack against the United States (Schwartz & Wald, 2003).

p124.original: 美国参议院情报委员会（U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee）在调查伊拉克战争的原因时，将“群体思维”作为导致该决策的原因之一。有趣的是，在该政府委员会的正式报告中，我们注意到了这种社会心理学概念的使用：
p124.en: The United States Senate Intelligence Committee (U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee) has identified “group thinking” as one of the reasons for this decision when investigating the causes of the war in Iraq. Interestingly, in the official report of the Government Commission, we noted the use of this concept of socio-psychology:

p125.original: 长期以来，情报界（The Intelligence Community，IC）一直在努力克服分析师的工作偏差。这种普遍存在于情报分析和收集过程中的偏差就是“群体思维”，这是心理学家欧文·贾尼斯在20世纪70年代创造的一个术语，用来描述当群体中的每个成员都试图使自己的观点符合群体共识时，群体可能会做出错误或非理性的决定的过程。参与伊拉克大规模杀伤性武器问题的情报工作人员展示了群体思维的几个方面：研究的替代方案很少，有选择地收集信息，存在群体压力或拒绝批评、集体合理化（U.S. Senate，2004，p.4）。
p125.en: The Intelligence Community, IC, has been working for a long time to overcome the bias in the work of analysts. This widespread bias in intelligence analysis and collection is “group thinking”, a term created by psychologist Owen Janis in the 1970s to describe the process by which a group may make erroneous or irrational decisions when each member of the group tries to bring its views into line with the group's consensus. Intelligence workers involved in Iraq's weapons of mass destruction issues have shown several aspects of group thinking: few alternatives to research, selective collection of information, group pressure or rejection of criticism, and collective rationalization (U.S. Senate, 2004, p. 4).

p126.original: 最近，美国情报局找到了一种方法，可以通过建立“红队”来最大限度地降低群体思维的风险，该团队的任务是以更可靠的证据挑战所有决策。其成员坚持收集多方来源的独立证据，以支持政府机构的所有行动决策。在重要情况下，企业、新闻机构、公司甚至陆军都使用红队扮演“魔鬼的拥护者”，尤其在时间紧迫、匆忙做决策的情况下。顾问丽莎·麦克劳德（Lisa McLeod，2013）表示，当决策风险很高时，即使是在我们的个人生活中，都应该使用红队方法。文身、初婚、参军、离婚，对于所有人来说后果都持续终身。在你抛弃配偶或者在前臂上刻上她的名字之前，请找一个更为年长、睿智、冷静的人询问：“你预见到了哪些潜在的负面后果？”当局者迷，旁观者清。
p126.en: Recently, the United States Intelligence Service has found a way to minimize the risk of group thinking by creating a “red team” whose task is to challenge all decisions with more reliable evidence. Its members insist on collecting independent evidence from multiple sources to support all operational decisions of government agencies. In important cases, businesses, news agencies, companies and even the army have used the Red Corps to play the role of “endorses of the devil”, especially in times of urgent and hasty decision-making. Lisa McLeod, a consultant, stated that the Red Team approach should be used even in our personal lives when decision-making risks are high. The consequences of tattoos, first marriage, military service and divorce continue for all. Before you abandon your spouse or mark her name on your forearms, ask someone older, wise and calmer: “What are the potential negative consequences that you have foreseen? "The authorities are fascinated, the bystanders are clear.

p127.original: 考虑一下你的行为的未来后果，并在第一时间获得一些友好的建议。
p127.en: Consider the future consequences of your actions and get some friendly suggestions at the first moment.

p130.original: 描述一下你在家里、学校、和朋友在一起或在工作中出现群体思维的时刻。
p130.en: Describe the moment when you are at home, at school, with your friends or at work in a group mind.

p133.original: 解释在各种情境下服从权威的力量。
p133.en: The power to interpret the submission to authority in all circumstances.

p134.original: 目前，我们已经强调了群体如何影响个人。但是影响力的箭头也指向了另一个方向：某些具有超凡魅力的领导者和权威人士，他们可以命令群体服从自己，甚至得到一大批人的拥护。在第二次世界大战时期，我们就可以看到这种效应的最极端证据，如德国的阿道夫·希特勒（Adolf Hitler）和意大利的贝尼托·墨索里尼（Benito Mussolini）。这些独裁者使整个国家的理性民众变成痴迷于征服世界的法西斯意识形态的忠实追随者。而当时英国新任首相温斯顿·丘吉尔（Winston Churchill）的理性镇定在关键时刻产生了影响，当时该国正处于被希特勒的导弹和德国空军不断轰炸的灾难边缘。1939年，丘吉尔以“保持冷静，继续前行”作为自己的座右铭。说来令人震惊，最近在海报、T恤和手机外壳上，这一座右铭开始复兴。
p134.en: At present, we have highlighted how groups affect individuals. But the arrows of influence also point in another direction: certain charisma leaders and authorities, who can order groups to obey themselves and even gain the support of a large number of people. During the Second World War, we saw the most extreme evidence of this effect, such as Adolf Hitler of Germany and Benito Mussolini of Italy. These dictators have turned the rational people of the entire country into faithful followers of fascist ideologies obsessed with subjugating the world. At that time, the rational calm of the new British Prime Minister, Winston Churchill, had an impact at a critical time, when the country was on the brink of a disaster that was being bombed by Hitler's missiles and by the German Air Force. In 1939, Churchill used the motto “Keep calm and keep moving” as his own motto. It is shocking that this motto has recently begun to recover on posters, T-shirts and mobile phone casings.

p135.original: 英国首相在第二次世界大战中的座右铭已经成为我们现代高压力生活中的口号。
p135.en: The motto of the British Prime Minister in the Second World War has become the slogan of our modern high-pressure life.

p136.original: 现代社会心理学起源于充满恐惧、偏见与残酷的第二次世界大战时期。因此，早期的许多社会心理学家自然会专注于研究法西斯主义群体中人们的人格。具体来说，他们在寻找法西斯群体心理背后的权威人格（Adorno et al.，1950）。但是，这种人格分析未考虑当时影响欧洲人的社会、经济、历史和政治现实。为了阐明这一点，让我们盘点一下在现代一些毫无异议地服从权威的例子。
p136.en: Modern social psychology originated in the Second World War, which was full of fear, prejudice and cruelty. Thus, many early social psychologists naturally focus on the human personality of people in fascist groups. Specifically, they are looking for the authority behind the psyche of the fascist community (Adorno et al., 1950). However, this personality analysis did not take into account the social, economic, historical and political realities that affected Europeans at the time. In order to make that clear, let us take stock of some examples of unchallenged submission to authority in modern times.

p137.original: 与服从权威有关的战后暴行 1978年，一群美国公民离开加利福尼亚（California），他们都信仰人民圣殿教（Peoples Temple），并在南美的圭亚那丛林中安营扎寨。在那里，他们听从了有超凡魅力的领袖吉姆·琼斯（Jim Jones）牧师的命令，近1000名人民圣殿教成员自愿对自己的孩子、父母和自己使用致命剂量的氰化物。这个邪教的成员还杀害了那些拒绝如此做的人，这些人彼此是朋友。
p137.en: In 1978, a group of American citizens left California, believed in the People Temple and camped in the jungle of Guyana in South America. There, they obeyed orders from a charming leader, Pastor Jim Jones, and nearly 1,000 members of the People's Temple Church volunteered to use lethal doses of cyanide on their children, parents and themselves. Members of this cult have also killed those who refused to do so, who are friends with each other.

p138.original: 然后，在1993年，在得克萨斯州的韦科（Waco，Texas），一个宗教教派的100名成员与他们的领导人大卫·科雷什（David Koresh）一起，对包围他们、搜查违规武器的联邦特工进行了反抗。经过数周的僵持后，大卫的信仰者们并没有投降，而是纵火焚烧自己的住所。大火中，数十名男子、妇女和儿童丧生。两年后，为了报复政府围困韦科的不当行为，蒂莫西·麦克维（Timothy McVeigh）和特里·尼科尔斯（Terry Nichols）对俄克拉荷马城（Oklahoma City）的一幢联邦大楼进行了恐怖袭击。威力无比的炸弹造成168人死亡，680多人受伤。爆炸摧毁16个街区范围内的324座建筑物，烧毁了86辆汽车，并炸碎了附近258座建筑物的玻璃，造成至少约6.52亿美元的损失。两年后，又有39名受过大学教育的自称为“天堂之门教”组织的成员在其首领的教唆下集体自杀，以实现“更高的生存境界”。此外，在2001年9月11日，本·拉登的追随者用武器劫持了美国民航客机，并驾驶它们撞向五角大楼和世界贸易中心。他们谋杀了数千人后，自杀身亡。甚至最近，在巴勒斯坦针对以色列和伊拉克的战役中，许多自爆袭击者都被炸得粉身碎骨，成了“革命烈士”。
p138.en: Then, in 1993, in Waco, Texas, 100 members of a religious sect, together with their leader David Koresh, resisted federal agents who surrounded them and searched for illicit weapons. After weeks of stalemate, David's believers did not surrender, but set fire to their homes. Dozens of men, women and children were killed in the fire. Two years later, in retaliation for the Government's wrongful actions in siege of Wako, Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols carried out a terrorist attack on a federal building in Oklahoma City. Unbridled bombs killed 168 people and injured more than 680. The explosion destroyed 324 buildings within 16 blocks, burned 86 vehicles and broke glass from 258 nearby, causing damage of at least $652 million. Two years later, 39 more members of the university-educated organization called themselves "The Gate of Heaven" committed suicide collectively, at the instigation of their leaders, in order to achieve a “higher survival”. In addition, on 11 September 2001, Bin Laden's followers hijacked American civil aviation passenger aircraft with weapons and drove them into the Pentagon and the World Trade Center. They committed suicide after murdering thousands of people. Even recently, in the Palestinian campaign against Israel and Iraq, many suicide bombers were blown to pieces and became “revolutionary martyrs”.

p139.original: 英国作家查尔斯·珀西·斯诺（C. P. Snow）提醒我们：
p139.en: The British writer Charles Percy Snow reminds us:

p140.original: 回顾人类漫长而阴暗的历史，发现以服从为名实施的骇人听闻的犯罪多于以叛乱为名。
p140.en: Looking back at the long and dark history of humanity, we find that more heinous crimes are committed in the name of obedience than in the name of rebellion.

p141.original: 犯下这些暴行的人是否精神错乱、愚蠢，或者与我们不同的特殊生物？在某些情况下你会盲目服从你所爱和尊敬或恐惧的人去执行这些极端的命令吗？例如，你会服从权威人物要求你对陌生人进行电击的命令吗？当然，你自认为：“不可能”“不是我”“我不是那种人”。但是，请思考一下在之前描述的实验中，每个人在掉入“服从陷阱”之前思考的问题可能都与你一样。
p141.en: Are the perpetrators of these atrocities insane, stupid or different from our particular creatures? Do you in some cases blindly obey those you love and respect or fear to carry out these extreme orders? For example, would you obey the orders of the authorities to electroshock strangers? Of course, you think, “No way” “not me”, “I'm not that kind of person”. But think about what you might think about in the experiment described earlier, before everyone falls into the “obligation trap”.

p142.original: 让我们回顾一下开篇的故事，即比尔在社会心理学家米尔格拉姆创建的实验（1965，1974）中的经历。该研究表明，人们会服从权威的命令，甚至可能是潜在的致使他人受伤的命令，这些人并不仅仅是少数极端人格或精神错乱的个体。这一发现及实验引发的伦理问题使米尔格拉姆的研究成为心理学界具争议的问题之一（Blass，1996）。稍后，我们将探讨有关服从的研究并从中得到更多发现，除此之外，我们还将讨论一系列后续研究，这些研究扩展了米尔格拉姆效应在日常生活环境的相关性和适用性。法国媒体在真人秀中也利用了这种效应。但是，首先让我们思考一下，为何这项研究中发现的高服从率使一些人类行为专家感到意外。
p142.en: Let us recall the opening story of Bill's experience in the experiment founded by the social psychologist Mirgram (1965, 1974). The study shows that people are subject to authoritative orders, and may even be potential orders to cause injury to others, and that these are not just a few individuals with extreme personality or mental disorders. This discovery and the ethical problems arising from the experiment made the Mirgram study one of the controversial issues in the psychology community (Blass, 1996). In addition to the studies we will explore later on on compliance and learn more from them, we will discuss a series of follow-up studies that expand the relevance and applicability of the Millgram effect in everyday life settings. The French media have also used this effect in reality shows. However, let us begin by thinking about why the high rate of submission found in this study surprised some experts in human behaviour.

p143.original: 11.3.1 回顾米尔格拉姆的研究

p144.original: 米尔格拉姆向40位精神病学家介绍了他的实验程序，然后要求他们估计在实验中会有多大比率的美国公民施加全部的30级电击。他们预测的比率只有不到1%，而且只有虐待狂才会如此做，大多数人会在电压到达第十级也就是150伏时退出。
p144.en: Milgram introduced 40 psychiatrists to his experimental procedures and then asked them to estimate the rate of the experiment at which United States citizens would be subject to full 30-degree electroshock. They predicted less than 1 per cent, and only sadists would do so, and most people would quit when the voltage reached level 10, or 150 volts.

p145.original: 他们的判断错得离谱！这些有关人类行为的专家犯错的原因有二。
p145.en: They're wrong! There are two reasons for these experts in human behaviour to make mistakes.

p146.original: 1. 他们忽略了实验程序中影响行为的情境决定因素；也就是说，他们没有意识到权威、老师与学生的角色、规则、个人责任的分散（实验者向“老师”声称自己将对可能发生的任何事情负责）、老师对适当行为的定义以及其他导致服从的社会压力的重要性。
p146.en: 1. They ignored the contextual determinants of behaviour in the experimental procedure; In other words, they are not aware of the authority, the role of teachers and students, the rules, the decentralization of personal responsibility (the experimenter claims to the “teacher” that he will be responsible for anything that may happen), the teacher's definition of the appropriate conduct and the importance of other social pressures that lead to obedience.

p147.original: 2. 他们过分依赖从性格角度来理解异常行为，这源自他们所接受的传统精神病学方面的训练，即从个人性格构成寻找解释，而非行为的外部情境。因此，他们估计只有1%的人会盲目服从权威，一直施加电压达到最大水平450伏，1%是一个基本比率，我们可以据此评估本研究中实际发生的情况。
p147.en: 2. They rely disproportionately on the understanding of abnormal behaviour from a personality perspective, which stems from their training in traditional psychiatry, i.e., the search for an explanation from the individual's personality composition rather than from the external context of behaviour. Thus, they estimate that only 1 per cent of the population will be blindly subject to authority, with a maximum of 450 volts and 1 per cent a basic ratio, against which we can assess what actually occurs in this study.

p148.original: 高估个人的力量和低估情境的力量的双重趋势被称为基本归因错误（Fundamental Attribution Error，FAE）。这是人类做出判断时常见的错误之一。
p148.en: The double trend of overestimating the power of individuals and underestimating the power of situations is called the basic attribution error (Fundamental Act Error, FAE). This is one of the common mistakes in human judgment.

p149.original: “电击设备”看起来恐怖，但实际上并没有给作为实验者同盟的“学生”（中图）施加电击。最后一张照片显示了实验者向坐在电击设备前的“老师”发出指示的过程。
p149.en: “Electro-shock equipment” appears to be horrific, but in practice it does not apply electric shocks to “students” (in the middle map) who are allies of the experiment. The last photo shows the process by which the experimenter gave instructions to the “teacher” sitting in front of the electroshock device.

p150.original: 社会心理学家认为，这种趋势限制了我们对社会情境在某种程度上会为某些行为提供重要解释的认识。当然，这并不是非此即彼的问题，但是通常在性格倾向和情境力量之间存在交互作用，使我们观察并想要理解的最终行为得以形成。这种人格-环境交互作用（person-situation interaction）是人格和社会心理学的核心，但是，很少有人研究在特定的社会环境中，对于特定类型的个体，每个因素对特定行为的相对贡献（Kihlstrom，2013）。
p150.en: According to social psychologists, this trend limits our understanding of the social context, which to some extent provides an important explanation for certain behaviours. Of course, this is not an issue of either side, but it is usually a interaction between character tendencies and situational forces that allows us to observe and understand the final act. This personality-environment interaction is at the core of personality and social psychology, but very few people study the relative contribution of each factor to a given behaviour in a particular social setting for a particular type of individual (Kihlstrom, 2013).

p151.original: 米尔格拉姆操纵了更多变量 米尔格拉姆还想证明他的结果并不是由于耶鲁大学的权威——这种权威就是纽黑文市的全部意义。因此，他将自己的实验室移到康涅狄格州布里奇波特市中心的一座破旧的办公楼中，并以一个虚构的私人研究公司的名义重复了该实验，该公司与耶鲁大学没有任何明显的联系。
p151.en: Milgram manipulated more variables, and Milgram wanted to prove that his result was not because of Yale's authority -- that's the whole meaning of New Haven. As a result, he moved his laboratory to a dilapidated office building in the centre of Bridgeport, Connecticut, and repeated the experiment in the name of a fictional private research company, which had no apparent connection with Yale University.

p152.original: 在那里，他测试了另外500名普通公民，并在实验中增加了女性被试作为老师。那么，在这些新情况下，盲目服从权威的实际比例是多少？
p152.en: There, he tested another 500 ordinary citizens and added women to the experiment as teachers. So what is the actual proportion of blind submission to authority in these new circumstances?

p153.original: 与在耶鲁大学进行的测试一样，布里奇波特的大多数被试都完全服从了权威：三分之二（65%）的人将电压施加到最大电击水平450伏！尽管“学生”曾绝望地要求停止，但这些“老师”却一次又一次地电击了他们的“学生”。无论这些“老师”是何年龄，是何种性别，教育水平如何，从事什么职业，结果都是如此。
p153.en: Like the tests conducted at Yale University, most of Bridgeports were tested in full compliance with the authority: two thirds (65%) of the people put the voltage at a maximum shock level of 450 volts! Although “students” had desperately demanded an end, these “teachers” had electric shocks to their “students” over and over again. This is true regardless of the age, sex, level of education and occupation of these “teachers”.

p155.original: 米尔格拉姆共进行了24个不同的实验。他每次都会在基础范式的基础上改变一个社会心理学变量，然后观察其对实验结果的影响。这些变量包括增加女性被试，控制实验者与老师或老师与学生之间联系的紧密程度，老师能否提前看到反抗或完全服从的例子，或者其他的社会变量。
p155.en: Milgram has conducted 24 different experiments. He changes a sociopsychological variable each time, based on a basic paradigm, and then looks at its impact on the results of the experiment. These variables include increasing the number of women tested, controlling the close connection between the experimenter and the teacher or teacher, whether teachers can see examples of resistance or complete obedience in advance, or other social variables.

p156.original: 如图11-4所示，16种变式的数据清晰地展示了人性极大的可塑性：在某些情境下，几乎每个人都可能完全抵抗权威的压力。这完全取决于特定的情境设置。
p156.en: As shown in figure 11-4, 16 variants clearly demonstrate the extreme plasticity of humanity: in some situations, almost everyone may be completely resistant to authoritative pressure. This depends entirely on the particular circumstances.

p157.original: 图11-4 米尔格拉姆实验

p158.original: 注：该图显示了米尔格拉姆服从实验在不同情况下对权威的服从水平。
p158.en: Note: The figure shows the level of submission of Mirgram to authority under different circumstances.

p159.original: 想要最大限度的服从？那么让新老师先观察其他人施加最大电击的情境。在这种情境下，米尔格拉姆观察到服从率急速上升到90%以上。
p159.en: Want maximum compliance? So let the new teacher first observe the situation where the maximum electric shock was inflicted by others. In this context, Mirgram observed a sharp rise in the compliance rate to over 90 per cent.

p160.original: 希望人们抵抗权威的压力吗？那么提供其他人反抗的例子，服从率将降低到10%以下。
p160.en: Want people to resist the pressure of authority? Then give an example of resistance from others, and the compliance rate will be reduced to less than 10 per cent.

p161.original: 如果学生说他想被电击，实施电击的被试也会拒绝进行电击；“那是受虐狂，我可不是虐待狂！”另外，当实验者作为学生进行实验时，他们也不愿给予高强度的电击。再者，与学生距离他们较近相比，当学生距离他们较远时，他们更有可能实施电击。在所有的变式中，被试包括年龄、职业和性别差异多样化的普通美国公民。一个简单的情境切换，就可以引发低、中或高不同水平的服从，仿佛在他们的心中转动了人性表盘。来自不同背景的普通公民的大量样本使米尔格拉姆的服从权威研究的结果在社会科学中变得更为全面。
p161.en: If the student says that he wants to be subjected to electric shocks, the test to perform them will also refuse to carry out electric shocks; "That's a sadist. I'm not a sadist! Moreover, when the experiment is conducted as a student, the experimenter is not willing to give a high-intensity electric shock. Moreover, students are more likely to undergo electric shocks when they are far from them than when they are closer to them. In all variants, ordinary United States citizens who have been tried to diversify their age, occupation and gender differences are included. A simple situational transition can trigger low, medium or high levels of obedience, as if a human dashboard had been turned around in their hearts. A large sample of ordinary citizens from different backgrounds has made the results of the Subordinate Authority study of Mirgram more comprehensive in the social sciences.

p162.original: 关于这些发现，我们要强调一点：无论我们是否意识到自己被观察，对于所有观察我们的人来说，我们都是强大的社会模范。当我们做坏事时，其他观察者可能会模仿我们，但是当我们像英雄一样行事时，我们将成为他人向善的榜样。因此，请注意你的行为引起的连锁反应，无论它是好的或坏的。
p162.en: With regard to these findings, we would like to emphasize that we are a strong model of society for all those who watch us, whether or not we are aware that we are being observed. When we do bad things, other observers may imitate us, but when we act like heroes, we will be role models for others. So, please note the chain reaction of your behavior, whether it's good or bad.

p163.original: 关于米尔格拉姆实验的思考 当然，学生从未遭受任何电击。“被电击”的“受害者”实际上是一位演技精湛的演员，在实验后他会与“老师”友好地聊天，使他确信自己安然无恙，并且从未受过任何电击。在实验开始前已录制了他在实验期间的所有台词，以使在不同的实验条件下研究的程序标准化。而且，身穿灰色实验室服装的权威人物不是“真正的”权威，也不是米尔格拉姆本人，而是一位高中生物学老师！而且，据这些“老师”所知，一旦学生在被施加330伏电击后保持沉默，他可能已经失去知觉或死亡，并且进一步的电击并不能改善他的记忆。即使毫无依据，数百人仍会盲目地服从。如果他们对所做的事情进行了理性和批判性的思考，应该已经意识到这项研究并不是要提高学生的记忆力，而是与他们相关，即让他们成为不情愿的惩罚的代理者。
p163.en: The thinking about Milgram's experiment, of course, the students never suffered any electric shocks. The “victim” of the “electric shocks” was in fact a skilled actor who, after the experiment, spoke amicably with the “teacher” and assured him that he was safe and had never been subjected to any electric shocks. All of his lines during the experiment were recorded before the experiment began in order to standardize the procedures studied under different experimental conditions. Moreover, the authority in grey lab clothes is not a “real” authority, nor Mirgram himself, but a high school biology teacher! Moreover, to the knowledge of these “teachers”, once the student remains silent after having been subjected to 330 volt electric shocks, he may have lost consciousness or died, and further electroshocks do not improve his memory. Hundreds of people will obey blindly, even if there is no basis for it. If they had thought rationally and critically about what they were doing, it should have been realized that the study was not intended to improve the memory of students but was relevant to them, i.e. to make them agents of reluctant punishment.

p164.original: 这些研究和之后世界各国的许多重复研究挑战了我们的假设，即“好人”不会被诱惑成为邪恶的犯罪者。它们表明善与恶之间的界限不是恒久不变的，而是可以跨越的。几乎任何人都可能从一个行为领域转移到另一个行为领域。这完全取决于他们所面临的且必须应对的新的、陌生的情境的力量。
p164.en: These studies and, subsequently, many repeated studies from around the world challenge our assumption that the “good people” will not be lured into becoming evil criminals. They show that the line between good and evil is not constant, but can be crossed. Almost everyone may move from one area of conduct to another. It depends entirely on the power of the new and unknown situations they face and must deal with.

p165.original: 在继续讨论反抗不公正权威的问题之前，需要提及最近发生的两次与米尔格拉姆有关的事件。一本享有盛誉的学术期刊的专栏刊登了文章“50岁的米尔格拉姆：探索心理学最著名实验的持久相关性”（Milgram at50: Exploring the Enduring Relevance of Psychology's Most Famous Studies，Haslam et al.，2014）。此外，2015年上映了一部有关米尔格拉姆的电影！斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的一生和他的全部研究都可以在好莱坞纪录片《实验者》（Experimenter）中看到。在这部纪录片中，米尔格拉姆由彼得·萨斯加德（Peter Sarsgard）饰演，他的妻子亚历山德拉（Alexandra）由女演员薇诺娜·瑞德（Winona Ryder）饰演，迈克尔·阿尔梅瑞达（Michael Almereyda）编导。
p165.en: Before continuing to discuss the issue of resistance to unjust authority, it is important to mention two recent incidents related to Mirgram. An op-ed in a well-known academic journal published the article “Mirgram 50: Exploring the Enrolling Relevance of Psychologic's Most Famous Studies, Haslam et al., 2014). In addition, a film about Milgram was released in 2015! Stanley Millgram's life and all his research can be seen in the Hollywood documentary Experimenter. In this documentary, Milgram was played by Peter Sarsgard, his wife, Alexandra, by Winona Ryder, an actress, and by Michael Almereyda.

p166.original: 追根溯源，斯坦利·米尔格拉姆和菲利普·津巴多是纽约市布朗克斯区的詹姆斯·门罗高中（James Monroe H. S.）的同学，他们于1950年毕业后继续研究提升情境力量的概念的方式。
p166.en: In retrospect, Stanley Millgram and Philip Zimbabwe were classmates at James Monroe H.S. High School in the Bronx, New York City, who continued to study ways to raise the profile of power after graduation in 1950.

p168.original: 情境的力量面临一个挑战：个体英勇的反抗。英雄（heroes）是那些能够抵抗令其他人服从的压迫性情境力量，并忠于个人价值观的人。他们是“检举人”，面对公司规范或机构标准操作程序，他们采取不附和的态度，并挑战腐败或不道德的系统。
p168.en: The power of the situation is challenged by the heroic resistance of individuals. Heroes are those who are able to resist oppressive situations that subject others to them and who are loyal to their own values. They are “prosecutors” who take an unconforming attitude and challenge corrupt or immoral systems in the face of corporate norms or institutional standard operating procedures.

p169.original: 陆军预备役人员乔·达比（Joe Darby）便在2004年成为这般英雄，他揭露了伊拉克阿布格莱布监狱（Abu Ghraib Prison）中对囚犯的残酷虐待的行为。他向一名高级调查官提供了一张光盘，其中有狱警在夜班时虐待囚犯的图像。随后该官员发起了调查，制止了持续数月之久的虐待行为。
p169.en: The army reservist Joe Darby became such a hero in 2004 when he exposed the cruel treatment of prisoners in Abu Ghraib Prison, Iraq. He provided a senior investigator with a CD-ROM containing images of ill-treatment of prisoners by prison guards during night work. The official then initiated an investigation to stop the abuse, which lasted for several months.

p170.original: 但是，这样的“英雄”经常被他们的前同事嘲讽，并且由于没有成为沉默的“团队成员”而付出高昂的代价。举例来说，因为曝光这些虐囚照片羞辱了美国军方，达比遭到了其营中的士兵和同乡人的死亡威胁，他不得不与妻子和母亲一起接受三年的保护性监视。在2007年解除监控后，他终于在华盛顿肯尼迪中心（Kennedy Center）获得了英雄奖。
p170.en: However, such “heroes” are often ridiculed by their former colleagues and pay a high price for not being a silent “team member”. For example, because of the exposure of these ill-treatment photographs to the United States military, Darby had been threatened with death by soldiers and his fellow inhabitants in his camp and had to undergo three years of protective surveillance with his wife and mother. Following his release in 2007, he finally won the hero prize at the Kennedy Center in Washington.

p171.en: Heroes come from all over the world.

p172.original: 在中国北京举办的2008年奥运会开幕式上，篮球运动员姚明牵着一个小男孩亮相。这个叫林浩的小男孩就读于四川的一所学校，地震时学校的屋顶发生了坍塌，他幸存了下来，但大多数学生没有那么幸运。在往外跑时，他注意到有两个孩子被压在废墟下，于是他回去救了他们。当被问到为什么要冒生命危险这样做时，林浩回答：“这是英雄的责任。”他说他是班长，照顾同学是他的职责。这是将同情心转变为英雄行为的一个很好的例子。我们对英雄主义行为的定义是：个体意识到潜在的个人风险或代价并且没有期望回报时，代表有需要的人或捍卫道义而采取的自愿行动。
p172.en: At the opening ceremony of the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing, China, basketball player Yao Ming held a little boy in his presence. The young boy, Lin Ho, was enrolled in a school in Sichuan, where the roof collapsed during the earthquake and he survived, but most of the students were less fortunate. As he was running, he noticed that two children had been trapped under the rubble, and he returned to save them. When asked why he risked his life to do so, Linho answered: “It is the duty of heroes. He says he's a class leader and it's his job to take care of his classmates. This is a good example of the transformation of compassion into heroic behaviour. We define heroism as voluntary action on behalf of those who need it or in defence of morality when individuals are aware of potential personal risks or costs and do not expect returns.

p173.original: 我们想为你阐述一个年仅17岁的巴基斯坦女孩马拉拉·尤萨夫扎伊（Malala Yousafzai）的鼓舞人心的故事，她的勇敢英雄行为使她赢得了2015年的诺贝尔和平奖。马拉拉喜欢读书和上学，直到塔利班（Taliban）开始关闭学校并禁止女孩读书或接受教育。在了解可能的后果后，她仍决定公开挑战这一对本国年轻人的发展造成限制的规定。马拉拉在塔拉班枪手的枪杀中幸存下来，在父亲的支持下，马拉拉在全球的媒体平台上继续反抗这种不公正的权威。如对此感兴趣，读者可自行上网搜索相关资源。
p173.en: We would like to share for you the inspiring story of a 17-year-old Pakistani girl, Malala Yousafzai, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2015 as a result of her brave heroism. Malala preferred to study and attend school until the Taliban (Taliban) began closing schools and prohibiting girls from studying or receiving education. After understanding the possible consequences, she had decided to openly challenge the provision that limited the development of young people in her country. Malala survived the shooting of Taraban gunmen and, with the support of her father, continues to resist this unjust authority on the global media platform.
